tags.name: WebhooksOverview
tags.description:
Webhooks are web requests that are made from our server to an endpoint configured by you, whenever certain events happen. You can create webhooks in the _integrations_ section of your account settings. Check out the [webhook guide](https://support.rentle.io/en/creating-webhooks) in our support center for detailed instructions on how to create webhooks using the web user interface. Alternatively, you can create webhooks by calling the [webhooks API endpoint](#tag/Webhooks).

Each type of event has its own endpoint, for example product creation, order update, etc. Identify which events you want to monitor, and create a webhook for each one.

Webhooks calls include the `x-rentle-version` header with the version that is used for the request body. The version is the one you have selected when creating the webhook.

Webhooks that we send expect a `2xx` response as an awknowledgement of reception. Any response code outside of that range, or a request timeout are considered a failure to deliver. Your receiving endpoint should quickly return a response code before any long-running logic happens on your server (e.g., writing to a database). Our webhooks requests will timeout after 10 seconds.

Receiving endpoints must use HTTPS.

In case of failure, webhooks are retried using exponential back off until one hour has passed since the event is delivered. After that, the webhook is not attempted again for that particular event.

We send webhooks from static IP addresses. This allows you to secure your receiving endpoints and allow requests only from these IP addresses. The IP addresses we send the webhooks from are:

- 34.78.116.141
- 35.205.39.8

### Limitations:

- Webhooks might be delivered more than once. Your receiving endpoint should check the `eventId` in the webhook request body and store it somewhere, to determine if a particular event has already been processed.
- Webhooks might be delivered out of order. For example, if an order is created and immediately updated, your system might receive the 'update' before the 'create' webhook. To circumvent this, we always send the full information of the target object. Your system should also implement checks and call the API whenever necessary to fetch any missing information.
- Delivery is not guaranteed. After a certain number of failed retries the webhook delivery is no longer attempted.

### Webhooks quick recap:

1. Identify the webhook events that you want to receive.
2. Implement the webhook endpoints on your target system, using HTTPS. Build your system in a way that it can handle receiving the same event multiple times, or out-of-order events. For instance, by checking the event id and discarding already-processed events.
3. Make sure your endpoint returns a response code in the `2xx` range.
4. Whitelist our egress IP addresses for added security.
5. Create the Webhook triggers via Rentle Admin or via the [webhooks API](#tag/Webhooks). Check that version of the API documentation that you use as a reference matches the API version of the webhooks that you create.

tags.name: Versioning
tags.description:
> **The API requires the `X-Rentle-Version` header to be provided for every endpoint.**

We use date-based versioning in the `yyyy-mm-dd` format for API versions. The version should be provided in every request using the `X-Rentle-Version` header.

Backwards-compatible changes and bug fixes are always a part of the same version. Breaking changes are always released in a new dated version of the API.

**The current API version is `2023-02-01`.**

## Release notes

### Planned changes for the future

Planned changes will be announced here before being released. A changelog of different versions will be maintained here as well.

### 2023-02-01

First version of the merchant admin API released. Allows reading resources from your merchant account.

## Legacy API

The documentation for our legacy API can be found from: https://api.rentle.io/docs. If you are still using the legacy API, we highly suggest to upgrade to this Rentle Admin API - all the new updates will be added only to this API.

tags.name: Authentication
tags.description:
### API keys

All requests are authenticated with a standard API key using HTTP Basic Authentication. If you already have a Rentle account, you can generate an API key on the [Integrations page](https://admin.rentle.io/account/integrations). Your API key will only be able to access data related to your own merchant account. The scopes that you select will determine which operations can be called with that key.

> Basic authentication is a simple authentication scheme built into the HTTP protocol. The client sends HTTP requests with the Authorization header that contains the word Basic followed by a space and a base64-encoded string username:password. For example, to authorize as demo / p@55w0rd the client would send `Authorization: Basic ZGVtbzpwQDU1dzByZA==`

The values for username and password are:

- `username`: Your API key ID
- `password`: Your API key secret

The API key secret will only be displayed once in the Admin UI. Take note of it and store it safely. Anyone who has the credentials can call the API on your behalf. In order to disable an API key you must delete it from the Admin UI.

### Scopes

When creating your API key, you will be asked to choose which scopes it has access to. It is recommended to only enable the scopes that you need that API key to be able to access, and add more scopes as required. An API key with all possible scopes enabled can be very destructive for your account if leaked to the wrong hands.

You can see the scopes required for each endpoint in the specific documentation page for the endpoint.

tags.name: RateLimiting
tags.description:
The Rentle API is rate-limited with a [Leaky bucket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leaky_bucket) system, where each API key has a "bucket" of API call quota available for their usage. This allows clients to make sudden bursts of requests without being rate-limited, so long as they are not consistently making more requests than the rate-limit allows.

You don't need to understand the algorithm very deeply, but to avoid being rate-limited you should simply make sure that a single API key is not, over a span of many hours, making more than 1 request per second.

More specifically, the relevant parameters for the leaky bucket algorithm are:

- Bucket maximum capacity: 50 requests
- Leak rate: 1 request per second (3600 per hour)

If you do exceed the rate limit, you will receive a `RateLimitExceedError (HTTP 429)` response. In this case, you must wait some time before being able to make requests again. If you require more requests for your application, you can contact our support team to upgrade your API quota.

tags.name: Feedback
tags.description:
Your feedback & bug reports are important for us to be able to develop the Rentle API further.

To give feedback, file bug reports and feature requests, notify us about an error in the documentation, or post a question about the API, head over to the [Rentle API feedback GitHub repository](https://github.com/rentle/rentle-api-feedback) to do so. Please note: this is not an official Rentle support channel, but more a channel for you to give feedback and receive assistance from either the Rentle dev team or other users of the API. If you need to chat with support, you should log in to your own shop at https://admin.rentle.io and use the official in-app support chat.

tags.name: Responses
tags.description:
The API responds with the following status codes:

| Status Code | Summary               | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ----------- | --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 2xx         | Success               | The API call was successful, and (usually) some payload was returned. Check each endpoint for specific details.                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| 400         | Bad Request           | The request was mal-formed and could not be processed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| 403         | Forbidden             | You do not have access to the resource that you are trying to access. The problem could be missing scopes, an expired/invalid API token.                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| 404         | Not Found             | The requested resource does not exist.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| 409         | Conflict              | The request has a conflict with the current state of the target resource. The problem can be caused when trying to delete an already deleted resource.                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| 429         | API Quota Exceeded    | You have reached the maximum number of API calls included in your plan. After a cooldown period you will be able to make API calls again. If this is a persistent problem, consider upgrading your plan to increase the number of included API calls. [See Rate Limiting](#tag/RateLimiting) for futher information about API call limits. |
| 500         | Internal Server Error | There was an unforeseen error in processing your request.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

Additionally, the response body will contain more information about the cause of the error in the following format:
